# Database audit: what each FAIL means and the fix

Run the audit (read-only) with `node scripts/db-security-audit.mjs`; each FAIL names one of the ids below.
Every fix is applied through the project's job route (a one-shot job on the VPS), after a backup, and only on the
owner's say-so. Nothing here has been applied. `NAME`/`HOST`/`TABLE` stand for what the FAIL printed.

| Check id | Severity | What it means | Fix | Where / how |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `acct.anonymous` | high | Anyone can connect without a user name; MariaDB then applies the anonymous account's rights. | `DROP USER IF EXISTS ''@'localhost';`<br>`DROP USER IF EXISTS ''@'%';` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); ops/db/hygiene.sql section 1 does this |
| `acct.empty_password` | high | An account that can be signed in to with no password. | `ALTER USER 'NAME'@'HOST' IDENTIFIED BY '<new secret, read from a file by the job>';`<br>`-- or, if nothing uses it: DROP USER 'NAME'@'HOST';` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); a new password goes in a root-only file, never in chat |
| `acct.wildcard_host` | medium | An account that accepts connections from any address ('%'), so only the network keeps it private. | `RENAME USER 'NAME'@'%' TO 'NAME'@'172.18.0.%';  -- use the subnet the host job prints for the database network` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); ops/db/grants.sql creates the narrow per-actor accounts (private host, connection limits) and ops/db/retire-old-account.sql then locks the old broad one |
| `acct.root_network` | high | An administrative account (ALL PRIVILEGES or SUPER) can log in from the network, not only from the server itself. | `DROP USER IF EXISTS 'root'@'%';  -- first confirm root@localhost works: docker exec <db container> mariadb -uroot -e 'select 1'` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); ops/db/drop-root-remote.sql (read its preconditions first) |
| `acct.powerful_privs` | high | A non-administrative account holds SUPER, FILE, PROCESS, SHUTDOWN, RELOAD, CREATE USER or GRANT OPTION: a stolen web password could read server files, see other queries, or mint new accounts. | `REVOKE SUPER, FILE, PROCESS, SHUTDOWN, RELOAD, CREATE USER ON *.* FROM 'NAME'@'HOST';`<br>`REVOKE GRANT OPTION ON *.* FROM 'NAME'@'HOST';` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); ops/db/grants.sql creates the narrow per-actor accounts (private host, connection limits) and ops/db/retire-old-account.sql then locks the old broad one |
| `acct.app_ddl` | medium | The web account can CREATE, ALTER or DROP tables; one SQL-injection bug then deletes the shop. The PHP never changes the schema at runtime. | `REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES, GRANT OPTION FROM 'NAME'@'HOST';`<br>`GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON sporta.* TO 'NAME'@'HOST';  -- exact set: the least-privilege lane's list in ops/db; run migrations as an admin job` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); ops/db/grants.sql creates the narrow per-actor accounts (private host, connection limits) and ops/db/retire-old-account.sql then locks the old broad one |
| `acct.unused` | low | An account with no rights to anything, or rights on a schema that no longer exists. (MariaDB records no last-login time; this finds accounts with nothing to use.) | `DROP USER 'NAME'@'HOST';` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); ops/db/grants.sql creates the narrow per-actor accounts (private host, connection limits) and ops/db/retire-old-account.sql then locks the old broad one |
| `acct.password_age` | low | A password not changed within the limit (default 365 days). | `ALTER USER 'NAME'@'HOST' IDENTIFIED BY '<new secret from a file>';  -- then update the secret file the application reads` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); rotate the web account together with its secret file |
| `srv.skip_grant_tables` | high | The server skips the permission system: every client is an administrator. | Remove --skip-grant-tables from the database service command (or my.cnf) and restart the database container. | the database service definition |
| `srv.network_exposure` | high | The database listens beyond the loopback interface, or a client is connected from a public address. Inside Docker it must listen on the container network, so the real test is on the host: 3306 must not be published. | Run the host job (ops/db/host-audit.compose.json) and confirm no port 3306 mapping.<br>If published: remove the "ports:" entry for 3306 from the database service and re-create it. | the database service definition + the host job |
| `srv.public_clients` | high | The server sees (or saw) a client connecting from a public IP address. | Find the source with the host job; remove any published 3306 port; DROP/RENAME the account it used to a private subnet host. | host job + a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) |
| `srv.skip_name_resolve` | low | Account host names are matched by DNS: slower, and a poisoned reverse lookup can change who matches which account. | Add skip-name-resolve under [mysqld] and restart. (Accounts must use IP/subnet hosts, not names.) | my.cnf, restart |
| `srv.local_infile` | medium | LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE is allowed: a malicious server or an injected statement can pull files from the client side. | `SET GLOBAL local_infile = 0;`<br>Persist: local-infile=0 under [mysqld]. | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf; ops/db/hygiene.sql section 3 |
| `srv.secure_file_priv` | medium | SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE and LOAD_FILE are not confined to a directory, so FILE privilege reaches anywhere the server can write. | Set secure-file-priv=/var/lib/mysql-files under [mysqld] and mount an EMPTY, read-only directory there (MariaDB refuses a path that does not exist, and has no NULL value); restart. | my.cnf, restart |
| `srv.sql_strict` | medium | Non-strict SQL mode silently truncates over-long values and coerces bad input instead of refusing it (the PHP does not set its own mode). | `SET GLOBAL sql_mode = 'STRICT_ALL_TABLES,NO_ZERO_DATE,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION';`<br>Persist: sql_mode=... under [mysqld]. | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf; takes effect for new connections |
| `srv.sql_zero_date` | low | Zero dates (0000-00-00) are accepted, which hides bad input. | Add NO_ZERO_DATE,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE to sql_mode (see srv.sql_strict). | same change as srv.sql_strict |
| `srv.sql_div_zero` | low | Division by zero returns NULL instead of an error. | Add ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO to sql_mode (see srv.sql_strict). | same change as srv.sql_strict |
| `srv.sql_group_by` | low | ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY is off, so ambiguous GROUP BY queries run and return arbitrary values. Turning it on can break a query: run the suites on a copy first (the eleven GROUP BY queries in dropin/php-store read as compliant). | Add ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY to sql_mode after the native suite passes against it. | same change as srv.sql_strict, last |
| `srv.event_scheduler` | low | Scheduled events run with their definer's rights and are a place to hide persistence; the shop uses none (host cron does the jobs). | `SET GLOBAL event_scheduler = OFF;`<br>Persist: event_scheduler=OFF under [mysqld]. | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf |
| `srv.password_policy` | low | No password-strength plugin is active, so a weak database password is accepted. | `INSTALL SONAME 'simple_password_check';`<br>`SET GLOBAL simple_password_check_minimal_length = 24;`<br>Persist: plugin_load_add=simple_password_check under [mysqld]. | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf; ops/db/hygiene.sql section 4 |
| `srv.audit_log` | low | Logins are not recorded, so a brute-force or a stolen-password login leaves no trace on the database side. | `INSTALL SONAME 'server_audit';`<br>`SET GLOBAL server_audit_events = 'CONNECT';`<br>`SET GLOBAL server_audit_logging = ON;  -- plus server_audit_file_rotate_size / _rotations so it cannot fill the disk` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf |
| `srv.symlinks` | low | Symbolic links inside the data directory are followed. | Add skip-symbolic-links under [mysqld]; restart. | my.cnf, restart |
| `srv.version_support` | medium | The server series is out of support (or about to be): no more security fixes. | Plan a major upgrade: dump (D3 lane backups), pull the newer image, restore on a copy, run the suites, switch. Within a series, pull the latest patch release. | the database service definition |
| `tls.available` | medium | The server has no TLS configured: everything between the shop and the database (orders, names, phones) crosses the network in clear. | Create a certificate and set ssl_cert / ssl_key / ssl_ca under [mysqld]; restart. | my.cnf + secret files, restart |
| `tls.require_secure_transport` | medium | TCP clients may connect without TLS. | Set require_secure_transport=ON ONLY AFTER the PHP connects with TLS (PDO ssl options). The current PHP does not, so enabling it first takes the shop down; see ops/db notes. | my.cnf, restart; needs a PHP change first |
| `tls.versions` | medium | TLS 1.0/1.1 are allowed. | Set tls_version=TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3 under [mysqld]; restart. | my.cnf, restart |
| `tls.cert_expiry` | medium | The server certificate has expired or expires within 30 days. | Issue a new certificate, replace the files, restart (or FLUSH SSL on 10.4+). | secret files + restart |
| `log.general` | high | The general query log is on: every statement, with every customer name, phone and address in it, is written to disk (or to a table). | `SET GLOBAL general_log = 0;`<br>Persist: general_log=0 under [mysqld]; delete the old log file after reading it. | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf |
| `log.slow` | low | The slow log is on; it stores statement text with literal values for slow queries. | `SET GLOBAL slow_query_log = 0;  -- or keep it only while tuning, in a 0700 directory` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) |
| `log.binlog_pitr` | low | No binary log: the best recovery is the last dump, everything since is lost. (Owner decision: with a handful of orders a nightly dump may be enough.) | Add log-bin=sporta-bin, binlog_format=ROW, binlog_expire_logs_seconds=1209600 under [mysqld]; restart. Pair with the backup lane's dump.<br>Or pass --accept log.binlog_pitr to record that you decided against it. | my.cnf, restart; decide with the backup lane |
| `log.binlog_retention` | medium | Binary logs are kept without a limit (or longer than 30 days). They contain every changed row, personal data included, and fill the disk. | `SET GLOBAL binlog_expire_logs_seconds = 1209600;`<br>`PURGE BINARY LOGS BEFORE NOW() - INTERVAL 14 DAY;` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf |
| `lim.connections` | low | max_connections is far above what a small shop needs; a flood allocates memory per connection. | `SET GLOBAL max_connections = 200;` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf |
| `lim.user_connections` | low | No per-account connection limit: one flooded account can use every connection slot and starve the admin. | `ALTER USER 'NAME'@'HOST' WITH MAX_USER_CONNECTIONS 60;  -- or SET GLOBAL max_user_connections = 60;` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); the accounts in ops/db/grants.sql carry their own limits |
| `lim.statement_time` | low | No statement timeout: one runaway or injected query can pin the CPU. | `SET GLOBAL max_statement_time = 60;  -- the shop's longest wait is a 10 s advisory lock` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf |
| `lim.wait_timeout` | low | Idle connections are kept for 8 hours, holding slots. | `SET GLOBAL wait_timeout = 600;` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf |
| `lim.packet` | low | max_allowed_packet is above 64 MiB; one request can make the server allocate that much. | `SET GLOBAL max_allowed_packet = 33554432;  -- hero photographs are the largest rows` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf |
| `cs.server_defaults` | low | New tables created without an explicit character set become latin1 (or another non-utf8mb4 set) and mangle Arabic. | Set character-set-server=utf8mb4 and collation-server=utf8mb4_unicode_ci under [mysqld]; restart. | my.cnf, restart |
| `cs.database_default` | low | The shop database's default character set is not utf8mb4. | `ALTER DATABASE sporta CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) |
| `cs.columns` | medium | Columns that are not utf8mb4 cannot hold Arabic or emoji: values are mangled or cut at the first 4-byte character, and mixed character sets enable comparison tricks. | `ALTER TABLE 'TABLE' CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;  -- back up first; text already stored as ? stays ?` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) |
| `cs.collation_mix` | low | More than one collation in the shop schema: joins can fail with "illegal mix of collations" and comparisons behave differently per table. | `ALTER TABLE 'TABLE' CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;  -- for each table listed` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) |
| `sch.engine` | medium | A table is not InnoDB: no transactions, no foreign keys, and it can be corrupted by a crash. | `ALTER TABLE 'TABLE' ENGINE=InnoDB;` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) |
| `sch.primary_key` | low | A table without a primary key cannot be safely replicated, de-duplicated or repaired row by row. | `ALTER TABLE 'TABLE' ADD COLUMN id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY FIRST;  -- or archive and drop it if nothing reads it` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) |
| `sch.foreign_keys` | low | foreign_key_checks is OFF globally, so the database stops enforcing the links between orders, items and accounts. | `SET GLOBAL foreign_key_checks = 1;`<br>Persist: remove foreign_key_checks=0 from the server config. | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + my.cnf |
| `sch.definers` | medium | A trigger, event, routine or view runs with the rights of a powerful account (or one that no longer exists): whoever can change or reach it borrows those rights. | `SHOW CREATE <TRIGGER\|VIEW\|EVENT\|PROCEDURE> name;  then recreate it with DEFINER = a low-privilege account (SQL SECURITY INVOKER for views).` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) |
| `sch.backup_copies` | low | Tables that look like copies, backups or leftovers of an old build sit in the live schema. They hold the same personal data as the real ones and nothing reads them. | Export them first (D3 lane dump), then: DROP TABLE `TABLE`; | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); the data scan says "do not drop" the old-build tables until the live storefront's source is found |
| `sch.other_databases` | medium | Other databases (especially test / test_*) are visible to this account; the stock "test" database is writable by everyone. | `DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS test;`<br>`DELETE nothing by hand: also DROP USER ''@'%'; (see acct.anonymous) and REVOKE any grant on test\_%.` | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); ops/db/hygiene.sql section 2 drops test |
| `sec.password_hashes` | high | A password column holds values that are not salted password hashes (plaintext, or a fast digest that can be cracked offline). | The PHP uses password_hash(); re-hash on next sign-in (password_needs_rehash) or force a reset. Never read the values to "fix" them. | application change |
| `sec.token_storage` | medium | A session/token/OTP column stores the value itself, so a database read (backup, SQL injection) yields live sign-ins. | Store sha256(token) in a token_hash column and compare hashes; invalidate the existing tokens. | application change (PHP patch), then delete old rows |
| `sec.hash_columns` | low | A column named like a hash holds values that do not look like one. | Check the column; if it is plaintext, rename and hash it as above. | application change |
| `sec.recoverable_secrets` | medium | A secret the server must be able to read back (an authenticator seed) is stored in clear in the database, so anyone with a database copy can generate valid codes. | Encrypt it with a key kept outside the database (PHP: sodium secretbox, key in the private config) and store 'enc:v1:...'; this check passes when every value carries that prefix.<br>Or pass --accept sec.recoverable_secrets to record the decision to live with it. | application change (PHP patch) |
| `sec.secrets_in_text` | high | A text/JSON column contains something shaped like "password: ..." / "token: ..." / "api_key = ...". | Find the rows with a SELECT limited to the key name, move the secret to the private config files, rotate it, blank the field. | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account) + rotation |
| `hyg.card_numbers` | high | Free text contains a number shaped like a payment card (13-19 digits, Luhn-valid). | `hyg.location_lines` | medium | Orders older than the limit (default 90 days) still carry the customer's precise map location in the note, and the privacy page does not mention location at all. | `UPDATE orders SET customer_note = TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(customer_note, '(Location\|الموقع): ?https://[^ ]+', '')) WHERE created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 90 DAY AND customer_note LIKE '%google.com/maps%';`<br>Same for fulfilment_outbox.payload; add the location line to Privacy.jsx section 1. | a one-shot job as an administrative account (never the web account); owner decision on the period |
| `hyg.retention` | low | The privacy page promises no retention period ("as long as we need them for accounting and for the returns period"), so there is nothing to measure against. ## UNKNOWN is not a pass

UNKNOWN means the connecting account cannot look, or the answer lives on the host. Re-run with an auditor account
(see HOST-CHECKLIST.md, "Full-visibility audit account") or run the host job. `--accept ID` records a decision to live with a FAIL;
it is printed as accepted and never counted as a pass.
